description:
A captured listing carries child names without per-child identity, so a mutation stops hashing directory entries it does not write.

## Background

A captured image carries, beside its file entries, a fingerprint of each discovered directory listing: the complete set of child names with their identities. Its purpose was to detect a sibling file appearing or vanishing between capture and commit. Archive planning and the shared command module read those listings as data — which children exist, under which directory — at nine sites, so name discovery stays; the per-child identity is what goes.

The race-detection guarantee is dropped deliberately. A mutation no longer detects a directory-entry race, and the repository write lock is what makes that acceptable for the files a mutation writes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No listing fingerprint type and no fingerprint accessor survives in the workspace, and a captured listing carries child names without per-child identity.
- [hard] REQ-02: Commands that consulted a listing as data still read the child names they need from the captured image.
- [hard] REQ-03: Capture byte and name budgets still bound what a listing read may consume, and a rogue directory still refuses the capture.
- [hard] REQ-04: The source-text policy assertion naming the fingerprint accessor is retargeted, with its reason stated where it lands.
- [hard] REQ-05: The change removes more lines than it adds.

## Notes

The budget coverage over oversized listings states a real property and survives.
title: Listing fingerprint retirement
